title: Ten Times and One Tenth
short: Each place is ten times the place to its right and one tenth of the place to its left.

blocks.html: In Grade 4 you saw that each place is worth ten times the place to its right, and you met tenths and hundredths. The same pattern runs both ways and keeps going past the decimal point.
Moving one place to the left makes a digit worth 10 times as much. Moving one place to the right makes it worth $\frac{1}{10}$ as much.

Ten ones make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Going the other way, cut one whole into 10 equal parts and each part is a tenth; cut a tenth into 10 parts and each is a hundredth. So every place is 10 of the place to its right, and $\frac{1}{10}$ of the place to its left.

blocks.name: placevalue
blocks.cap: Every digit is a 5, but each 5 is worth 10 times the 5 to its right: $500, 50, 5, 0.5, 0.05$.

blocks.title: Ten times as much
blocks.q: In $4{,}444$, compare the 4 in the hundreds place with the 4 in the tens place.
steps: The hundreds 4 is worth $400$. The tens 4 is worth $40$.
blocks.a: The hundreds 4 is worth 10 times as much.

blocks.title: Across the decimal point
blocks.q: In $7.77$, compare the 7 in the tenths place with the 7 in the hundredths place.
steps: The tenths 7 is worth $0.7$. The hundredths 7 is worth $0.07$.
$0.07 \times 10 = 0.7$, so the tenths 7 is worth 10 times as much.
Turned around: the hundredths 7 is worth $\frac{1}{10}$ of the tenths 7.
blocks.a: 10 times as much (or $\frac{1}{10}$ as much, the other way)

blocks.title: Two places apart
blocks.q: In $3{,}030$, how many times as much is the 3 in the thousands place as the 3 in the tens place?
steps: Thousands are two places left of tens.
Each place is a factor of 10: $10 \times 10 = 100$.

blocks.html: Thinking a digit further right is worth more because it is “bigger” or comes later. In $0.55$, the first 5 (tenths) is worth 10 times the second 5 (hundredths). Check by writing each value: $0.5$ and $0.05$.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, 5.NBT.A.1: a digit in one place represents 10 times what it represents in the place to its right
